summary: Fragmented rate attribution across preview and production postbacks causing fractional invoice lines
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightLens reported unexpected small invoice lines (fractional cents) for a billing period after a canary rollout. Charges appear as multiple micro-line items attributed to the same logical job: some postbacks are listed under a preview key (preview-*) and others under production key (prod-*). The combined quantity matches expected usage, but the rate applied to preview postbacks differs (lower rate class) leading to split-line billing and confusion on final invoice.

Impact:
- Customer saw ~0.03 USD fragmented lines across 120 invoice rows for a single batch run; total is correct but the breakdown is confusing for accounting and triggers their finance alerts.
- Customer finance has requested an explanation and a consolidated invoice view; they are enterprise tier and asked for expedited response.

Environment:
- Prod: us-east primary. Mixed routing to eu-west fallback for some micro-batches during canary rollout window 2026-03-08T22:00:00Z - 2026-03-09T03:30:00Z. Models: open-embed-v2 used for preview embeds; open-chat-medium used for production chat preview endpoint.

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Run batch job with preview flag enabled for small percentage of requests (preview-mode header).
2) Route traffic through canary alias that splits to both preview and prod postback pipelines.
3) After job completes, view invoice line-items in Console -> Billing -> Detailed usage.

Observed behavior:
- Postback events from the same logical request were ingested under two different rate keys depending on which pipeline processed the acknowledgment (preview vs prod).
- Billing service applied different rate classification for preview keys (trial/preview tariff) which produced fractional per-request lines.

Expected behavior:
- Same logical request should reconcile to a single rate key based on org-tagging and final routing decision; preview postbacks for production traffic should not be charged under preview tariff.

Logs / Evidence:
- Customer provided a CSV of 127 affected request IDs and corresponding postback timestamps, plus a screenshot of Console invoice lines (attached in Jira comment).
- Billing ingest trace for sample request id brl-20260309-xyz shows two postbacks within 2s with different tag sets.

Notes:
- This ticket is related to previous postback-ordering and canary mixing reports (see linked issues).
- Customer requests: 1) explanation of why two rate keys were used, 2) consolidated invoice or provisional credit for the fractional lines, 3) steps to prevent recurrence.

investigation_notes: Root cause hypothesis: postback-ingest pipeline assigns rate keys at the time of ingestion using tagset that can include ephemeral 'preview_mode' header. For a small fraction of requests, subsequent reconciliation (which runs later) merges postbacks but did not update the rate-key grouping for invoice line aggregation, leaving two distinct rate-buckets. Repro in staging: enabling preview header + induced fallback routing yields duplicated line keys. Proposed fix: change rate-key derivation to run during final reconciliation and ignore ephemeral preview flags for billing classification unless org explicitly in preview tier. Patch PR 982 changes precedence order and adds reconciliation idempotency checks.
resolution:
Provisionally credited customer $12.30 to offset accounting noise (credit id CR-20260312-BRL). Engineering deployed a canary patch (postback/PR/982) that normalizes rate-key derivation during reconciliation; canary evaluation window complete with no regressions. Plan: rollout patch to all postback-ingest nodes in next maintenance window (2026-03-14 02:00 UTC). After rollout, billing will run a reconciliation pass for 2026-03-08..2026-03-10 to collapse duplicate micro-lines. Final confirmation and invoice adjustment to be posted as a follow-up comment.

Follow-ups assigned:
- Billing: run reconciliation job and prepare invoice adjustment (owner: Marcus Nguyen).
- Postback team: monitor canary metrics and push full rollout (owner: Elena García).
- Support: confirm customer can import consolidated CSV after adjustment (owner: Aisha Patel).
resolution_notes: Patch merged to main in PR 982. Canary metrics: preview-mode-tagged postbacks reduced to <0.02% of ingests with split attribution during canary. Reconciliation dry-run collapsed 121 micro-lines to single lines for provided sample set. Credit issued and ledger updated. Billing will include final adjustment on next invoice cycle; customer requested an interim consolidated CSV which was uploaded to ticket attachments. Ticket to remain open until reconciliation completes and customer confirms import success.
customer_communication_plan: Notify customer within 24h of full rollout. Provide consolidated CSV and link to credit entry. Follow up to confirm GL import succeeded and offer one-off invoice reissue if needed.
